jobs.title: Environmental Analyst or Associate Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**Environmental Analyst or** **Associate Environmental Scientist**
==================================================================

* Location: Richmond, California
* Program: Clean Water
* Type: Full-time
* Experience Level: Entry Level
* Position Type: Permanent
* Salary: $87,500 to $98,500

Position Description
====================

* Posted: November 19, 2026
* First review of applications: December 4, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
* Application Close Date: The position will close on December 18, 2026 or when 150 applications have been received, whichever occurs first.

The San Francisco Bay Nutrient Management Strategy (NMS) is expanding its modeling program, with new work on harmful algal blooms, nutrient load-reduction scenarios, and coastal–Bay coupling. The San Francisco Estuary Institute (SFEI) seeks an early-career environmental engineer or scientist to carry out modeling investigations related to nutrient cycling, phytoplankton dynamics, and dissolved oxygen in San Francisco Bay and the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta.

Modeling will support the NMS (http://sfbaynutrients.sfei.org/), a multi-year science program that studies the effects of nutrient inputs on the Bay and evaluates potential management actions. The NMS modeling team has developed a coupled hydrodynamic-biogeochemical model of the full Bay, now entering its second decade of development. The model recently completed external review by a Model Advisory Group of independent experts who identified dissolved oxygen and harmful algal bloom (HAB) prediction as the next priorities.

The successful applicant will share responsibility for application of the model within a team of hydrodynamic and biogeochemical modelers. Near-term projects include improving the representation of dissolved oxygen, sediment processes, and phytoplankton physiology; running scenarios that evaluate load reductions and environmental changes; testing HAB and toxicity modules with the NMS HAB Modeling Workgroup; running scenarios with the Bay model to inform a coastal ocean model under a newly funded Ocean Protection Council project with UC Santa Cruz, UCLA, and the Southern California Coastal Water Research Project; and supporting water quality modeling in the Delta.

The team works regularly with researchers at the U.S. Geological Survey, Deltares, and other academic and agency partners. Results feed into technical reports, peer-reviewed publications, and materials for the NMS Steering Committee and regulators. This is a hybrid role based in the Richmond office, where regular in-person presence supports team collaboration and access to the modeling computing infrastructure. We strongly prefer this position to be a hybrid role based in the Richmond office. Fully remote arrangements may be considered depending on the candidate.

Primary position responsibilities will include:

* Running the biogeochemical model for a wide variety of projects load reduction, nutrient trading, source apportionment, and environmental change scenarios.
* Conducting parameter exploration experiments to test model sensitivity.
* Comparing model output against NMS monitoring data (moored sensors, ship-based mapping, discrete samples, satellite imagery).
* Maintaining reproducible scripts and workflows for input preparation, post-processing, and plotting of model results.
* Preparing results in technical reports, Steering Committee and advisory group materials, and peer-reviewed articles.
* Exploring science questions within the Program's modeling scope, including HAB dynamics, coastal export of nutrients, and system progression under possible futures.
* If you are excited about this role, but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this, or one of our other roles.

Qualifications

No field work or lifting is required.

Required Experience
-------------------

* Bachelor's degree +2 years of experience in civil and environmental engineering, oceanography, quantitative ecology, applied mathematics, or a related field with relevant environmental coursework in hydrodynamic or biogeochemical modeling, or
* Master's degree +0 years of experience in civil and environmental engineering, oceanography, quantitative ecology, applied mathematics, or a related field with relevant environmental coursework and/or masters thesis focused on hydrodynamic or biogeochemical modeling.

Relevant experience includes using hydrodynamic or biogeochemical models in biological, chemical, or physical oceanography, biogeochemistry, ecology, or civil and environmental engineering. Experience with estuarine, coastal ocean, lake, or reservoir modeling is particularly relevant.

Required Skills
---------------

* Educational background or coursework in numerical modeling demonstrating an understanding of foundational hydrodynamics and/or biogeochemistry
* Strong analytical and data analysis skills in Python, Matlab, R, or a similar language, including developing post-processing tools, plotting methods, time series analysis, and data cleaning
* Excellent oral and written communication skills, including experience communicating scientific findings to a broad audience and working with a wide range of collaborators
* Ability to work on multiple projects and work both independently and as part of a team
* Interest in learning new skillsets, new applications, and new systems

Preferred Skills
----------------

* Experience working with Python or Jupyter Notebooks
* Experience with the Delft3D FM / D-Water Quality suite or another unstructured-grid model
* Familiarity with Linux and version control (git)
* Experience handling large gridded or unstructured model output (netCDF, xarray) and running jobs on a shared computing server or cluster
* Model calibration, sensitivity analysis, or uncertainty quantification
* Experience modeling d

jobs.title: GHD Graduate Program 2026/27 – Environmental Science (Planning/Impact Assessment) – Melbourne
jobs.description:
**We’re GHD.**

We don’t do hair. But we do straighten out some of the world’s biggest challenges.

We’re engineers, scientists, designers, architects, planners, advisors, innovators and change makers, committed to making energy, water and communities sustainable for generations to come.

Since 1928, we’ve been wholly owned by our employees. Today, we are 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals working in over 160 offices across five continents — Asia, Australia, Europe, North and South America, and the Pacific region.

  

Who could you be at GHD?

Our **Planning & Impact Assessment team** based in **Melbourne** supports projects through the environmental planning and approvals process, helping identify and manage environmental impacts and risks. The team brings together environmental scientists, planners, engineers and environmental specialists to support projects through assessment, approvals and delivery.

The team is looking for a **Graduate Environmental Scientist** to join our Graduate cohort, commencing in either **February** or **July 2027** .

We’re looking for someone who:

* has recently graduated (or is a current student expecting to graduate by the end of 2026, or mid-2027) with a degree in **Environmental Science, or a related environmental discipline**
* has an interest in **environmental planning, impact assessment and environmental approvals**
* is keen to develop experience in environmental investigations, data collection and analysis, environmental impact assessments and technical reporting
* has an interest in understanding environmental risks, regulatory requirements and sustainable project outcomes
* has great verbal and written communication skills and enjoys working collaboratively in a multidisciplinary environment.
  

Our two-year Graduate Development Program is designed to give you a smooth start to your consulting career. Alongside your peers, managers and mentors, we’ll help you detangle any challenges along the way. You’ll be mentored by senior aquatic ecologists with decades of experience across Australia, and build skills in survey techniques, field safety, animal ethics requirements and technical reporting that will set you up for a long career in aquatic science.

**A frizz-free application process:**

#WeDontDoHair but we do want your journey to be as smooth as possible, so here’s everything you need to help you prep like a pro:

* **Your CV:** This gives us a snapshot of what you’ve studied and your experiences, both paid and unpaid.
* **A cover letter:** Think of this as your chance to show us where you’d love to grow within GHD, while letting your communication skills shine.
* **Your transcript:** This helps us understand what you’ve been learning, from your core subjects to the electives that sparked your curiosity.

**Your journey to joining GHD:**

Here’s what to expect, step by step:

* **Screening:** We review applications as they come in, but be mindful that the bulk of our screening happens after applications close, so don’t worry if you don’t hear from us right away.
* **Virtual Assessments:** If you make it through the first stage, you’ll record some answers to a few straightforward questions and complete some cognitive games. This helps us get a better sense of your work style and alignment to GHD
* **Meet the team:** If you’re successful, you’ll have a face-to-face interview (wherever possible) with your prospective team. We’ll chat through some behavioural questions to learn more about your skills and experience. It ’ s also a chance for you to get to know us!
* **Offer:** Congratulations! We’ll talk through all the finer details, like salary, your start date, our onboarding process and what to expect before your first day.

We’re committed to being as inclusive as possible and giving everyone an equitable chance of getting through our application process. **If you identify as someone who is neurodiverse or have a disability** and need adjustments to any part of the process, let us know in your application form—we’re here to help.

  

**Ready to shine?**

If you’ve got your documents polished and prepped, the application should only take 10-15 minutes. Apply now and take the first step toward an exciting career in consulting.

**If you’ve previously applied for this position, there’s no need to reapply.**

**GHD: The Power of Commitment**

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

Community impact is important to us, influencing how we work, our projects and how we give back. Our *GHD in the Community* program partners with not-for-profit organisations so that we can work on pro-bono projects, as well as volunteering and fundraising for philanthropic and humanitarian causes. As a business, we also channel some of our profits into the *GHD Foundation* *,* a registered charity that addresses disadvantage and inequality in children accessing STEAM education in the countries where we live and work.

Within GHD, our employee groups and networks help us foster community, find our tribe, and celebrate what makes us unique. These groups play a big part in our global diversity, equity and inclusion strategy, creating spaces for meaningful and safe conversations, connecting with likeminded individuals, and creating a voice to leadership.

#LI-JN1

jobs.title: Team Leader, Remediation Quality Control
jobs.description:
**Team Leader, Remediation Quality Control**
============================================

**Date:** 19 Nov 2026

**Location:** Sydney, Australia

**Company:** Singtel Group

Optus is an Australian telecommunications company, delivering more than 11 million services to our customers every day across mobile, broadband and digital solutions.

At Optus, we're committed to delivering fair and customer-focused outcomes. We're currently seeking a **Quality Control Team Leader, Remediation** to lead a high-performing quality control team responsible for reviewing customer remediation cases and ensuring decisions are accurate, evidence-based, and aligned to regulatory obligations.

  

**What You’ll Do**

Reporting to the Director, Remediation Operations & Partnerships, you'll lead the quality review process across complex remediation matters, ensuring customer outcomes are fair, well documented, and able to withstand governance and regulatory scrutiny. You'll coach and develop a team of quality specialists while driving continuous improvement across assessment quality, consistency, and compliance.

**Key responsibilities-**

* Lead quality reviews to ensure remediation outcomes are fair, accurate, and compliant.
* Coach and develop a team of quality specialists, driving consistency and continuous improvement.
* Provide feedback and facilitate calibration sessions to improve assessment quality and decision-making.
* Identify quality trends, emerging risks, and opportunities to enhance processes and controls.
* Escalate complex matters through appropriate governance channels.
* Foster a high-performing, inclusive team culture.
* Partner with stakeholders across Operations, Risk, Compliance, and Legal to deliver strong customer outcomes.
  

**What makes you perfect for the role?**

You bring strong quality assurance, remediation, complaints, audit, compliance, or regulatory experience and have a proven ability to lead and develop teams in complex environments. You're comfortable making evidence-based decisions, navigating ambiguity, and influencing stakeholders at all levels.

You'll also have:

* Experience leading, coaching, or developing teams.
* Strong analytical and decision-making skills.
* Experience operating within compliance, risk, governance, or regulatory frameworks.
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
* A customer-focused mindset with a commitment to fairness, accuracy, and ethical conduct.
  

**What’s in it for you?**

* Competitive remuneration and employee discounts. Make life easier (and more affordable) with $80 monthly credit and 25% off Optus products and unique shopping discounts with our retail partners.
* Flexible working arrangements with opportunities to work three days in the office, two days remote or home.
* Vibrant and collaborative office campus that includes cafes, convenience store, chill out zones, GP, post office, gym and on-site childcare centre.
* Competitive leave policies, including additional 'Connected’ days to focus on culture, family, health, community, or whatever’s important to you.
* We support growing families with inclusive, carer-neutral paid Parental Leave of up to 16 weeks.
* Direct your own development and build future-ready skills with Optus U’s industry-focused micro-credentials, developed with La Trobe and Macquarie Universities.
* Build meaningful connections through employee-led networks and diversity initiatives including Culture Connect, Elevate Women, Disability Network and Express Yourself (LGBTQIA+).
* Put your wellbeing first with free access to counselling and support services, 24/7 — in-person, by phone, SMS, or video.
* Free Optus bus from Macquarie University Metro Station (every 6-8 minutes); morning and afternoon.
  

At Optus, we are strengthened by others and that means valuing diversity and saying ‘yes’ to embracing individual differences. We are committed to ensuring that our application process provides an equal employment opportunity to all job seekers, including individuals from diverse gender, cultural and linguistic backgrounds, individuals with a disability, individuals identifying as being part of the LGBTQIA+ community, individuals who may have served in the armed forces or who identify as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander. We also want to do our best to make our recruitment process inclusive. If you require any adjustments or accessibility support to participate fairly and equitably in the recruitment process, please email AccessibleRecruitment@optus.com.au or call 1800 309 170.

For more information on Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging at Optus, please visit https://www.optus.com.au/about/inclusion-diversity
